changes.text: 讲这场以少胜多的仗，可以只讲赢家的招数；这篇想说的是另一件事：一条被否决的建议，和赢家打赢之后怎样对待提建议的人。

A battle won against the odds can be told through the winner's tricks alone. This one is about something else: a proposal that was rejected, and how the winner treated the man who made it after the fighting stopped.
韩信和张耳带着数万人，准备东下井陉去打赵国；赵王歇和成安君陈馀把军队聚在井陉口，号称二十万。兵力对比一目了然，难处在另一头：据赵营中李左车的分析，汉军是乘胜离国远斗，粮食势必落在后面。就在交手之前，他向陈馀递上一条非常具体的方案，方案没有被采纳。这一篇要说的就是这条被否掉的计，以及打赢之后，赢家怎样对待出计的人。

Han Xin and Zhang Er were marching east with tens of thousands of troops, bound to attack the state of Zhao through Jingxing. King Xie of Zhao and the Lord of Cheng'an, Chen Yu, massed their forces at the Jingxing pass under a strength they claimed at two hundred thousand. The disparity was obvious. The trouble lay elsewhere: as Li Zuoche, in the Zhao camp, saw it, the Han army was riding its victories far from home, and its grain was bound to fall behind. Before the two sides came to blows, he put a very specific plan to Chen Yu, and the plan was turned down. This piece is about that rejected proposal, and about how the winner treated the man who drew it up once the fighting was over.
李左车给出的方案因此很具体：请拨奇兵三万人，抄小路断掉汉军辎重；主力深沟高垒，坚守不出战。汉军向前无仗可打、后退无路可走，后路被断、野外无处征粮，他估计不至十日，「兩將之頭可致於戲下」。他最后还留了一句警告：否则，「必爲二子所禽矣」——必定会被这两个人擒住。

His proposal followed from that. He asked to be lent thirty thousand picked troops to cut the Han baggage train by the side roads, while the main body held behind deep ditches and high walls and refused battle. Ahead the Han would have no one to fight; behind them no way back; with their rear cut and nothing to forage in the open country, he reckoned that in less than ten days the heads of the two generals could be delivered to the commander's tent. He closed with a warning: otherwise, he said, you will surely be taken by those two.
赵国这边的主帅成安君陈馀，史书对他的定性只有一句：「儒者也，常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。他拒绝的理由也被记了下来，是两层：一是算术，兵法说十倍可以围、倍数可以战，韩信号称数万、其实不过数千，千里奔袭已经疲惫到极点；二是名声，如果这样还避而不击，「則諸侯謂吾怯，而輕來伐我」。他没有采纳广武君的计策。

Chen Yu, the Lord of Cheng'an and Zhao's commander-in-chief, gets one line of characterization from the historian: a Confucian, who always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. His grounds for refusing are recorded too, in two layers. One is arithmetic: the manual says ten-to-one besieges, two-to-one fights; Han Xin claims tens of thousands but has no more than a few thousand, and a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone. The other is reputation: to avoid battle at such odds would mean, in his words roughly, that the lords would think him cowardly and come lightly to attack him. He did not take the Guangwu Jun's advice.
韩信先派人暗中探看，得知那条计没被采用，探子回报，他「大喜」，这才敢引兵下井陉，在离井陉口三十里处宿营。到夜半，他选出轻骑二千人，每人带一面红旗，抄小路到山上隐蔽观察赵军，并交代任务：赵军见我军退走，必然全营出动追击，你们就迅速进营，拔掉赵旗，插上汉军的红旗。这支骑兵此后的全部作用，取决于一个前提——赵军真的会倾巢而出。

Han Xin sent men to spy out the camp and learned the plan had not been adopted. When they reported back, he was overjoyed, and only then did he dare lead his army down toward Jingxing, halting thirty li short of the pass. At midnight he chose two thousand light cavalry, each man carrying a red banner, and sent them by side paths to hide in the hills and watch the Zhao army, telling them that when Zhao saw the Han withdraw, it would empty its camp to pursue; they were then to go in fast, pull down the Zhao banners and stand up Han's red banners in their place. Everything this detachment did later hung on one premise — that the Zhao army really would come out.
韩信派一万人先行而出，背靠河水列阵。赵军望见，「大笑」。按诸将事后引用的兵法，布阵要右背山陵、前左水泽。作者推测，背水列阵违背了这条常规，赵军或因此发笑；但原文只记了大笑，没有说他们笑什么。

He sent ten thousand men ahead; they went out and formed up with their backs to the river. The Zhao army saw them and roared with laughter. By the manual his generals later quoted, a proper line kept hills at the right rear and water at the left front. The author's guess is that this breach of the rule is what drew the laughter; the text records only that they laughed, not why.
平旦，韩信打出大将的旗鼓，擂鼓出井陉口，赵军开营出击，双方打了很久。然后韩信、张耳假装丢下旗鼓（原文「詳弃鼓旗」），退向水边的部队；水上那一军把他们放入阵中，回身再战。赵军果然全营出动，争抢汉军的旗鼓，一路追击韩信、张耳。而已退入水边阵中的汉军人人殊死作战，打不垮。

At dawn Han Xin raised the general's banners, beat the drums, and came out through the pass. The Zhao camp opened and attacked, and the fighting went on a long time. Then Han Xin and Zhang Er made a show of abandoning their drums and standards and fell back toward the force by the water, which opened its ranks to take them in and turned to fight again. The Zhao army duly poured out of its walls, scrambling for the Han drums and standards, chasing Han Xin and Zhang Er. The Han soldiers at the riverbank, Han Xin and Zhang Er now among them, fought to the death and could not be broken.
然后是这一篇真正关心的那一幕。韩信下令军中不得杀害广武君李左车，能活捉者赏千金。于是有人把捆着的李左车送到帐下，韩信亲自给他解开绳索，请他东向而坐、自己西向相对，以师礼待他。一支军队刚刚获胜，主帅下的命令里有一条，是保住对方那位出主意的人，还为此悬赏千金。

Then comes the scene this piece is really about. Han Xin ordered that the Guangwu Jun, Li Zuoche, must not be killed, and set a thousand in gold on bringing him in alive. Someone delivered him bound to headquarters; Han Xin untied him, seated him facing east while he himself sat facing west, and treated him as his teacher. An army had just won, and among the commander-in-chief's orders was one to keep the other side's adviser alive — with a reward of a thousand in gold for it.
接着韩信向李左车请教：我想北攻燕、东伐齐，怎样才能成功？李左车推辞，说自己是败军之将、亡国之臣，不足以议大事。韩信举了百里奚的例子：百里奚在虞国而虞亡，在秦国而秦霸，不是他在虞就笨、在秦就聪明，而是「用與不用，聽與不聽也」。他接着说，如果成安君听了您的计，我已经被擒了；正因为没有用您，我才有机会在此陪坐请教。

Han Xin then asked Li Zuoche: I mean to strike Yan in the north and Qi in the east — how do I make that work? Li Zuoche declined: a defeated general cannot speak of courage, a minister of a ruined state cannot plan survival; what am I, a captured and ruined man, to weigh great matters with? Han Xin offered the story of Baili Xi, who saw Yu fall while he served Yu and saw Qin rise to hegemony while he served Qin: not that he was foolish at Yu and wise at Qin, but that his advice was used or not used, heeded or not heeded. And had the Lord of Cheng'an heeded your plan, a man like me would already have been taken. It is because he did not use you that I sit here asking.
李左车开口说的是：「智者千慮，必有一失；愚者千慮，必有一得」，所以有句话说，狂夫之言，圣人也从中择取。一种解读是：一位刚刚亡国、被生擒的人，开口先讲的，近乎是任何人都可能出错——而他同时也说了，愚者也会有所得。

Li Zuoche began with the saying that the wise man, in a thousand considerations, must have one failure, and the fool, in a thousand considerations, must have one success — hence the saying, the sage still picks through a madman's words. One reading is that a man whose state had just fallen, taken alive, opened by suggesting that anyone can be wrong — while also allowing that even a fool can be right.

把原文所记陈馀拒绝的理由拆开看，会发现它们不是一类东西。「兵號數萬，其實不過數千」「千里而襲我，亦已罷極」是对敌情的判断，可以争论；“避而不击，诸侯就会说我怯懦”不是对汉军的判断，是对自身形象的判断。此外，史家在记这些理由之前，先交代了他平日的立场：「常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。这是司马迁对他一贯说法的描述，不是他这一次拒绝时给出的理由；而且它不是判断，是一条规矩。一种解释是：这条规矩与李左车的奇兵之计正好相冲，二者或有关联，但原文并没有把它记为这次拒绝的理由。作者推断，这也是为什么原文要给陈馀加上「儒者也」这个身份标签——史家记的是立场，不只是失策。

Split apart the reasons the text records for Chen Yu's refusal and they are not the same kind of thing. Claims tens of thousands, really no more than a few thousand; a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone — those are readings of the enemy, contestable in principle. Refuse battle and the lords will think me cowardly is not a reading of the Han army at all; it is a reading of his own image. Before recording those reasons, the historian also sets out his habitual stance: he always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. That is Sima Qian's description of what Chen Yu habitually said, not a reason he gave for this refusal; and it is not a judgment at all but a rule. One explanation: that rule runs directly against Li Zuoche's surprise-force plan, and the two may be connected, but the text does not record it as a ground for this refusal. The author's inference is that this is why the text labels Chen Yu a Confucian: the historian is recording a stance, not merely a mistake.
还有一个容易被忽略的不对称。战后诸将问的是“为什么背水”，也就是问赢家的招数妙在哪里；原文没有记下有人问“那条计当初为什么没被采纳”。作者推断，复盘天然聚光在胜者的技巧上，因为技巧可学；而一次否决看上去毫无技术含量，也不产生任何战果。可作者认为，这场仗里决定性的动作恰恰发生在开战之前——一次拒绝，和一次对拒绝的探知。

There is also an easy-to-miss asymmetry. After the battle the generals asked why the backs-to-the-water formation — a question about what made the winner's move clever. The text does not record anyone asking why that plan had not been adopted before the fighting. The author's inference: after-action review naturally spotlights the winner's technique, because technique can be learned, while a veto looks like it takes no skill and yields no result. Yet in the author's view, the decisive acts in this battle happened before the first blow fell — a refusal, and the discovery of that refusal.
现代虚构场景之二：一次交接。竞标赢了之后，甲方请的顾问，偏偏是对方阵营里那位方案被否的人——不是羞辱，是把他的思路当成课程。当年韩信解缚、师事李左车，做的就是这件事：赢家最值得问的，常常不是自己的谋士，而是对手那边没被听的那个。

Second modern scene, fictional: a handover. Having won the bid, the client hires as consultant precisely the person on the losing side whose plan was voted down — not to humiliate him, but to treat his thinking as coursework. Untying the bonds and serving Li Zuoche as a teacher is exactly that: the person most worth asking is often not your own adviser, but the one on the other side who went unheard.
本文唯一史源为司马迁《史记·淮阴侯列传》。其中人物对话是史家记述，未必逐字；「誠令成安君聽足下計，若信者亦已爲禽矣」出自韩信之口，属事后自述，不可检验。除原文所记理由外，本文未对陈馀的心理作任何补充；作者提出的替代情形只用于分析，不作事实陈述。

The only historical source for this piece is Sima Qian's "Account of the Marquis of Huaiyin" in the Records of the Grand Historian. The speeches there are the historian's account and need not be verbatim; "had the Lord of Cheng'an heeded your plan, a man like me would long ago have been taken" comes from Han Xin's own mouth, an after-the-fact statement that cannot be tested. Beyond the reasons recorded in the original text, this piece adds nothing to Chen Yu's psychology; the alternative scenario the author offers serves analysis only and is not stated as fact.

dispositions.rationale: 说明“常称义兵不用诈谋奇计”是史家对陈馀一贯说法的描述，不是这次拒绝的理由；它与拒绝之间的关联放进“一种解释是”；删去与所列内容不符的“两层”计数。英文同步。
